newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil output rose to 3.14 in January.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil output rose to 3.14 in January.

text.p: Norway pumped 3.14 million barrels per day (bpd) in January, up from 3.10 million bpd in December as some fields returned to normal output following disruptions, a Reuter survey of operators on the Norwegian shelf showed.

Statfjord, which suffered a 14 percent drop to 333,541 bpd in December from November because of well maintenance and a two-day shutdown, pumped an average 363,232 bpd in January, according to operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) .
Norsk Hydro's Oseberg and Brage developments were also back to normal levels after various problems in December knocked output down.
Saga Petroleum reported production at Snorre up at 235,841 bpd in January from 194,994 in December.
"We are simply doing very well," a spokeswoman said. "We expanded capacity at Snorre in the beginning of December. Now production is in full swing."
British Petroleum said the Ula and Gyda fields had reached peak production and would gradually drop during the year.
But production at Ekofisk, operated by Phillips Petroleum, fell to an average 255,505 bpd following a week-long shutdown caused by a gas leak in an oil pipeline in mid-January.
In December, technical difficulties and minor shutdowns made Ekofisk production slip to around 315,000 bpd from nearly 330,000 bpd in November.
As in December, the January figure omits production from the Sleipner condensate developments.

Operator Statoil said total liquid output -- stabilised oil and liquefied petroleum gases -- at Sleipner East and West amounted to 154,729 bpd, but the company was unable to provide a figure for condensate alone because of technical difficulties.
